front.title: PACE: Protocol for Agent Communication Exchange

abstract.t: This document defines the Protocol for Agent Communication Exchange (PACE), an agentic dialog management protocol with a binding to Media over QUIC Transport (MOQT). A dialog is the correlated sequence of interactions between two or more participants over the course of a task. PACE defines a transport-independent dialog context and control operations to establish, modify, and terminate dialogs and to revoke propagation relationships. It specifies how that context stays coherent across intermediaries, trust boundaries, modality changes, and interruptions, and how it is carried over MOQT. PACE does not interpret or define dialog content. Over MOQT, a dialog can combine text, audio, video, and request/response exchanges in point- to-point, point-to-multipoint, and multi-party topologies. Application-layer agent protocols such as A2A, MCP, and AutoGen keep their own message formats and carry the dialog context through their own extension points.
